sources.title: Generalizable Robotic Insertion with World Models
sources.publicationCheck: The arXiv record lists IROS 2026 in Comments. A separate proceedings publication record was not verified; content labels the reviewed version an arXiv preprint and attributes the venue note to the authors.
verifiedClaims: InsertionWM is a system using TD-MPC2 visual model-based RL, rather than a newly proposed base RL algorithm.
Inputs include wrist-camera depth images and proprioception; actions are end-effector pose changes selected through latent-space planning.
All experiments are conducted in simulation with a Franka Panda configuration.
The dataset contains 100 assembly pairs. The last 10 by asset ID are held out; they are unseen geometries from the same distribution.
The generalist trained on 90 pairs reports up to 56% zero-shot success over the held-out pairs, with 100 trials per assembly.
The study reports occlusion sensitivity and discusses depth-sensor noise, contact-simulation mismatch and real-time processing as obstacles to physical deployment.
cautions: Do not describe the 56% result as real-robot success or unrestricted out-of-distribution generalization.
Avoid an unqualified 56% versus 7% superiority claim: the text acknowledges that the precise AutoMate splits are unknown and that the observation interfaces differ.
No official code or weights were verified.

sources.title: World Models for Robotic Manipulation: A Survey
sources.publicationCheck: The reviewed arXiv record provides no verified conference or journal publication reference. The content labels this a survey preprint.
checkedSections: II Definition and Scope of World Models
verifiedClaims: A survey with three organizing questions: what future representation is predicted, how prediction connects to action, and when prediction is used.
The paper discusses five representation families and reviews 34 principal manipulation datasets.
The evaluation discussion distinguishes predictive fidelity, downstream task performance and simulator reliability.
The paper identifies contact-rich evaluation, metric fragmentation, action-conditioned calibration and closed-loop exploitation as benchmark gaps.
The conclusion calls for non-visual signals including force and tactile streams, alongside tests of physical credibility and action alignment.
cautions: The first submission was 27 May 2026 despite the identifier beginning 2606.
The survey does not provide a newly trained model, a new controlled experiment or a single comparable leaderboard.

sources.title: World Model for Robot Learning: A Comprehensive Survey
sources.publicationCheck: The reviewed arXiv record lists 43 pages and 6 figures in Comments, with no verified conference or journal publication reference. The content labels this a survey preprint.
verifiedClaims: The review covers world models for policies, as learned simulators, and for robotic video generation, with navigation and driving as additional applications.
Its policy taxonomy includes decoupled, single-backbone, mixture, unified VLA and latent-space approaches.
It collates benchmark results including LIBERO, RoboTwin, CALVIN and SIMPLER-style evaluations without presenting those results as a new controlled experiment.
Section 7.3 explicitly cautions against strict ranking across heterogeneous embodiments and protocols.
Challenges include weak action conditioning, latency and training costs, non-visual sensing and the lack of a widely accepted evaluation metric.
